title: What Elon Musk Really Thinks About Sam Altman
the_thought: He wanted the chair. Sam kept it.
hook:
A long table sits in a glass loft. One tall wooden chair stands at the head. Nobody is sitting in it yet. Elon Musk wants that chair. Later, Sam Altman sits in it. Two friends, one lab, and one chair. That is the fight.

He wanted the chair. Sam kept it.

Why would Elon want a wooden chair? He already had Tesla. He already had SpaceX. He already had rockets and cars. The chair was the boss chair at OpenAI. OpenAI was going to build talking machines. Whoever sat in that chair would steer those machines.

So watch the chair. Watch who asks for it. Watch who says no. Watch who sits down. Watch who leaves. Watch who builds a second table next door.

We cannot see inside Elon's head. We cannot see inside Sam's head. There is no secret diary in this video. We have mail. We have posts. We have a lawsuit. We have OpenAI's own later blog. Those papers are loud enough.

The title asked what Elon really thinks about Sam. A feeling you cannot point at. A chair you can. So the story starts with wood, not a birthday. Keep the picture. Two men. One seat. A long fight that starts in 2015 and ends with a clock in 2026. Every chapter is one step. First they share the table. Then Elon asks to sit. Then the scientists say no. Then he leaves. Then Sam sits. Then the talking box gets famous. Then Elon builds a table next door. Then a jury says he waited too long. If you can retell those eight steps, you can retell the video. That is the whole map. Do not get lost in the jokes. Do not get lost in the magazines. Stay on the wood.

levels.name: Honest Thoughts
beats:
December 2015. OpenAI starts. It is a nonprofit lab. Nonprofit means the lab is supposed to help everyone, not just the people at the table. Elon Musk and Sam Altman are co-chairs. Two bosses. Two names on the door.

TechCrunch said other rich helpers had pledged about 1 billion dollars. A pledge is a promise. A promise is not a pile of cash on the table. Why does that matter? Because later they would fight about money. The first big number was a promise, not a bag.

The lab needed brains more than balloons. Ilya Sutskever came to run the science. Greg Brockman came to build the code. Sam was the people person from Y Combinator. Elon was the famous one with Tesla and SpaceX.

For a little while it looked like a group hug in a glass loft. It was not a group hug. It was a table with one extra-tall seat. Two men both liked to drive.

We still cannot see inside their heads. What we can see is the next paper.

In 2017 the lab got scared. The computers would cost billions. Some of them talked about turning the nonprofit into a for-profit, so they could raise more cash. That is when the chair fight got sharp. Who would be CEO? Who would own the stock? Who would get to say go, or stop, if the machine got too smart?

September 12, 2017. OpenAI later published this. Elon laid out a board plan. He would unequivocally have initial control of the company. Those are his words in their exhibit. Initial means at the start. Control means the chair.

A September 4 message OpenAI published said he sounded fairly non-negotiable on equity between 50 and 60 percent. That is more than half. If you own more than half, you pick the slices. If you pick the slices, you pick who sits.

Sam wanted a path too. The scientists were stuck in the middle.

September 20, 2017. Ilya and Greg wrote a long email. The subject line was Honest Thoughts. Honest means they had not said the hard part yet.

They told Elon they worried about an AGI dictatorship. AGI is a future machine that can do almost all the brain jobs. Dictatorship means one person never has to share.

They said the goal of OpenAI is to make the future good and to avoid an AGI dictatorship. They also said they were afraid to speak earlier. Afraid of harming the relationship. Afraid of losing the famous partner.

Then they said something even sharper. They believed the nonprofit had worked because both Elon and Sam were in it. Sam acted as a genuine counterbalance to you, they wrote to Elon. Counterbalance means a second weight. If one person is much heavier, the other person never gets a turn. They thought Sam was the other weight. They thought they were worse at being that weight.

They also asked Sam hard questions in the same letter. Is AGI truly your primary motivation? How does it connect to your political goals? So the scientists were nervous about both men. This is not a cartoon where Sam is only an angel. This is a cartoon where the lab did not want either grown-up to own the future.

Why put that in a video about what Elon thinks of Sam? Because Elon's later story is that Sam took the mission. The 2017 mail shows Elon reaching for the chair first. Sam standing in the way. The scientists scared of both.

What does Elon really think about Sam in that week? The mail does not say he hates Sam. It shows a tug. Elon wants the chair. Sam will not hand it over. The scientists call Sam a counterbalance. A counterbalance is useful. A counterbalance is also in the way.

He wanted the chair. Sam kept it. The 2017 mail is the first time the chair is loud.

Hold one more simple question. If the scientists feared a dictator, why would they ever offer anyone a king chair? Because they also feared being too small to buy the computers. Fear of a king and fear of being poor can sit in the same week. That is why the email is called Honest Thoughts. They had been hiding the fear. Then they dumped it on the table.

levels.name: Final Straw
beats:
Elon answered Honest Thoughts fast. Minutes, not months. He called it the final straw. Final straw means he is done talking. He said discussions were over. He said they should go do something on their own, or stay a nonprofit. He said he would no longer fund OpenAI until they made a firm commitment to stay. Else, he said, he was just a fool giving free money for someone else's startup.

That last bit is a sulk and a threat in one sentence. Two famous men were fighting like kids over a clubhouse. One said you are not the boss. The other said then he was taking his money home.

OpenAI later said Elon even formed a Delaware company with a long stiff name, Open Artificial Intelligence Technologies, as a for-profit shell. Then the team would not give him unilateral control. Unilateral means only his hand on the wheel. So he walked. That is OpenAI's telling.

Elon's later telling wears a different costume. In that costume, he was the nonprofit helper and Sam was the pirate. Both costumes cannot be the whole truth at once. The 2017 paper trail is why. If you demand more than half the company and the CEO seat, you are not only a helper. If you later turn the lab into a giant money engine with Microsoft, you are not only a monk.

The funny part is they both wanted a big machine. They fought about whose name would be on the head chair.

January 2018. OpenAI says Elon told them the lab would fail unless it merged into Tesla. Tesla would be the cash cow. The team said no. Why would a rocket-and-car company swallow an AI lab? Because Elon already had a big vehicle that could raise money. The others did not want to live inside that vehicle. Merge means the Tesla boss is the real boss. The wooden chair moves to a car factory. Sam would not be the head of that table. So they refused.

February 2018. Elon resigns as co-chair. OpenAI's public blog blamed a future conflict with Tesla's own AI work. That is a clean public sentence. The private 2017 thread is messier. Both can be true at once. Tesla was chasing self-driving brains. And Elon had already lost the control fight.

February 20, 2018. A goodbye all-hands. Picture a tall man in a black shirt standing up from the long table. The wooden chair is empty for a second. Then other people keep meeting. Sam stays.

In 2019 Sam becomes CEO. The chair is no longer a maybe. Sam sits. Elon is outside the glass.

How much money did Elon actually put in? This number has costumes too. He once talked like it was 100 million dollars. Later reporting showed that balloon was too fat. In the later court fight he used about 38 million dollars for 2016 to 2020. OpenAI has said his help was under 45 million dollars. So pick a kid sentence. He gave tens of millions. He did not give a hundred million. He also paid some rent and even handed over a few Tesla cars, in his telling. He later called himself a fool for giving free money. That is a bruise talking. A bruise is not a full history. But it tells you the feeling he wants the world to hear. He paid. They sat. He left.

Tens of millions is a lot of money. It is not ownership of the lab if the lab rules never gave him the chair. He wanted the chair. He did not get the chair. He got a donor thank-you and a goodbye.

After he left, OpenAI built a capped-profit arm in 2019. Capped-profit means you can make money, but there is a lid. Microsoft put in a first billion, then later much more. More than 10 billion dollars in the big deal people talked about around 2023. Later counts of Microsoft's pile ran even higher, more than 13 billion dollars in 2026 roundups. Exact later totals move. The point does not move. The lab found a giant piggy bank that was not Elon. Sam found that piggy bank. Elon watched from outside.

What does a person think about the friend who kept the chair and then found a bigger piggy bank? The emails from 2017 already told you. He thinks that friend blocked him. He thinks the mission got sold. OpenAI thinks he is rewriting the clubhouse rules after he quit the club.

OpenAI also says it offered Elon a slice of the later for-profit and he said no. If that is true, he did not want a visitor's stool. He wanted the head seat or nothing. That matches the 2017 control mail better than it matches a simple donor story. A donor can be happy with a thank-you card. A person who demanded 50 to 60 percent is not looking for a card.

The goodbye blog was polite. The later lawsuit was not. Polite and furious can be the same man on two dates.

levels.name: Talking Box
beats:
November 30, 2022. OpenAI turns on ChatGPT. A talking box on the internet. You type. It talks back. School kids paste homework. Office people paste emails. The box becomes famous in days.

Elon is not in the building. Sam is the CEO. The boom happens on Sam's watch. That timing is the joke the universe wrote.

Elon spent years warning that AI could be dangerous. He helped start the lab. He left. Then the lab's box became the most famous product in the category. If you are Elon, that can feel like watching your old lab invent the hit toy after you took your money home. If you are Sam, that can feel like proof the team was right to keep the chair.

Elon says the lab broke a promise. The promise, in his lawsuit later, was that the tools would be for humanity, not a private jackpot, and not a Microsoft exclusive. GPT-4, he complained, sat behind a paywall and a special door for Microsoft.

OpenAI says it needed huge computers. Huge computers need huge cash. And Elon himself had once pushed a for-profit. So who moved? Both, if you are honest. The nonprofit clubhouse grew a money floor. Elon grew a grudge. Sam grew a company.

The talking box is not a villain. The talking box is a magnet. Magnets pull money. Money pulls fights.

What does Elon really think about Sam in the ChatGPT year? Look at what he did, not a made-up whisper. He mocked the safety talk when it sounded, to him, like a costume. He said OpenAI had become a closed money shop. He said the name Open was a joke if the model weights stayed shut. That is an opinion about Sam even when the sentence says OpenAI. Sam was the face. Sam did the Senate rooms. Sam did the product launches. When Elon points at the lab, the finger lands on the man in the chair.

Is that fair? Fair is a school word. The papers are mixed. ChatGPT was built by a lot of people. Ilya. Greg. Engineers whose names never trend. But titles make cartoons. CEO is a cartoon job. The public treats the CEO as the whole factory. Elon knows that trick. He uses it for Tesla. He hates it when someone else uses it for his old lab.

Why? Because the old lab still wears a story that includes his name. He helped start it. He did not get to keep it. The talking box made the loss loud. Before ChatGPT, OpenAI was a smart loft. After ChatGPT, OpenAI was the thing on every phone. Losing a loft hurts. Losing the thing on every phone hurts in a different key.

Did Sam trick him? Elon says yes, in court language. OpenAI says no. Look at 2017. You wanted the for-profit and the wheel. A kid can hold both sentences. Sentence one: Elon wanted the chair and did not get it. Sentence two: Sam later ran a lab that made a lot of money with a giant company partner. Sentence three: we cannot know if Sam smiled in a secret room. Do not invent the smile. Invented smiles are how bad videos get made. Stick to the chair.

The chair moved from shared, to fought-over, to Sam's, to famous. The talking box also changed the audience. Before, the fight was emails in a loft. After, grandmas knew the product name. A loft fight can stay private. A phone fight cannot. Elon is good at phone fights. Sam is good at stage fights. Two styles. Same chair.

Why did ChatGPT make Elon louder about Sam, not quieter? Because the hit made the missed seat look more expensive. A missed seat in a quiet loft is a sulk. A missed seat under a famous box is a legend he does not want Sam to own alone.

levels.name: Five Days
beats:
November 17, 2023. OpenAI's board fires Sam Altman. The public note said the board no longer had confidence he was consistently candid. Candid means telling the full true thing. They did not list the full true thing. The company exploded anyway. Greg walked. Workers wrote a letter. Microsoft scrambled. For about five days the chair was empty again. Empty like 2018, but louder, because now the talking box was famous.

What did Elon do? He did not sit quietly. He posted. He said the public should be informed why the board felt it had to take such drastic action, given the risk and power of advanced AI. That sounds like a safety dad. It is also a man leaning over the old lab fence.

He backed Ilya. He said Ilya has a good moral compass and does not seek power. He said Ilya would not take such drastic action unless he felt it was absolutely necessary.

Remember 2017? Ilya helped write Honest Thoughts against Elon's control. In 2023 Ilya helped push Sam out. Elon liked that Ilya. Same Ilya. Different year. Different target. That is a twist a kid can track. The scientist who did not want Elon as dictator also did not want Sam unchallenged.

Then the workers pulled Sam back anyway. Five days. November 22, Sam is returning as CEO. New board promises. Old board gone. The wooden chair gets a cushion again.

Elon has mixed feelings, he said at a summit that week. Mixed is a real word. It is also a fog. Mixed can mean told-you-so. Mixed can mean he wanted Sam gone. Mixed can mean he liked the chaos. We do not have a mind reader. We have posts. The posts enjoy the mess. They demand an explanation. They praise Ilya. They do not say he will come back and sit down. He already had another table by then. We will walk to that table in a minute.

Why do the five days matter for what he thinks of Sam? Because when the chair wobbled, Elon did not write poor Sam. He wrote tell us the secret. He treated the firing as evidence that something was rotten in Sam's shop. That is a thought. Not a hug. Not a funeral. A flashlight pointed at Sam's face. Then Sam survived the flashlight. Surviving makes the grudge hotter, not cooler. If your old partner almost loses the chair and then gets it back with a parade, you do not think the universe agreed with you.

A funny sourced bit: people joked that Sam got fired on a video call. Elon piled on with office-movie jokes. That is playground behavior with a billion-dollar toy. The toy still belonged to the other kid when the weekend ended.

The board learned a lesson too. The workers liked Sam more than they liked a vague safety coup. Elon liked the coup more than he liked Sam. That split is the opinion. He thinks Sam's grip on the lab was the problem. The staff thought Sam's grip was the product.

Five days is a tiny number next to 2017. Why give it a whole chapter? Because it is the only time after 2018 the chair actually wobbled in public. Elon did not get invited to sit. Microsoft even floated a landing pad for Sam. The workers chose Sam anyway. If Elon thought the lab would finally agree with him, the parade home was the opposite lesson. The lab picked the man in the tan sweater. Not the man at the fence. Not the scientist with the moral-compass post. The tan sweater sat back down. The fence stayed a fence.

levels.name: Next Door
beats:
July 12, 2023. Elon announces xAI. A new lab. A new table. Months before the five-day fire drill. So when he leaned over the OpenAI fence in November, he was not a retired coach. He was already the owner of a rival clubhouse.

Grok, the chatbot, showed up on November 4, 2023, right as OpenAI was about to melt. Two talking boxes. Two tables. One city. Next door is the simplest picture. He could not sit in Sam's chair. He built another chair and dared people to sit with him instead.

xAI's pitch was maximally truth-seeking, not politically correct. That is Elon-speak. It is also a poke at Sam's shop, which Elon treats as a manners machine. Grok was supposed to be funnier and less of a hall monitor. Whether it was better is a product fight. This video is not a scoreboard for chatbots. This video is a chair story. The next-door table exists because the first table said no.

Then the poke got expensive. In 2025 a Musk-led group offered about 97.4 billion dollars to buy control of OpenAI's nonprofit parent. That is not a coffee. That is trying to buy the whole lab after you already built one next door.

Sam posted no thank you. Then he joked that they would buy Twitter for 9.74 billion if Elon wanted. Twitter here means X, the bird site Elon already bought.

Elon posted swindler. He also posted Scam Altman. Those are schoolyard names. They are also the clearest public words he has aimed at Sam as a person, not just at OpenAI as a logo. Swindler means cheat. Scam means fake. That is what Elon wants you to think Sam is.

Is that proven? A nickname is not a verdict. A 97 billion dollar bid is not friendship. A joke about buying X is not peace. It is two boys trading dares across a fence. One dare is buy the lab. The other dare is buy the bird. Neither dare closed. Sam kept the chair. Elon kept the insult.

What Elon really thinks about Sam, if we only use the loud public layer, is this. He thinks Sam is a smooth talker who took a charity and turned it into a money castle. He thinks the name Open is paint. He thinks Microsoft is the real landlord. He thinks he, Elon, was the one who cared about the future remote. Sam's camp thinks Elon wanted the remote for himself in 2017 and is now throwing rocks because he lost.

You do not have to pick a hero to see the shape. The shape is a chair, a no, a second table, a buyout dare, and a mean nickname.

Why not stop at the nickname? Because nicknames are cheap. The expensive part is the copycat lab. Starting xAI is the action that matches the feeling. If you still liked Sam, you would not spend a fortune cloning his toy. If you only disliked the board, you would not name-call the CEO. He did both. That is a full thought, even without a diary.

Next door also explains the 97 billion dare. You do not offer a mountain of money for a lab you think is holy and fine. You offer it if you want the keys. Keys are just the chair with extra metal. Sam's no-thank-you was a joke and a wall. Elon's swindler reply was a stamp on Sam's forehead. We still do not put that stamp in the court record as a finding. We put it in the opinion pile, where it belongs. Opinion plus action. Action plus insult. Insult plus a second talking box named Grok. Grok is not this video's hero. Grok is the toy on the other table, waving at ChatGPT like a sibling who wants the same bike.

levels.name: Too Late
beats:
February 29, 2024. Elon sues Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and OpenAI. The complaint says they broke the founding deal. It says the charity was supposed to belong to humanity. It says Microsoft got a special door to GPT-4. It is a legal way of saying you stole my clubhouse.

The case hopped into federal court in Oakland. For weeks in 2026 there was a trial with famous witnesses and a thick stack of old emails. Kids would call it a very long show-and-tell. Grown-ups called it Musk v. Altman.

What did Elon want the jury to believe about Sam? That Sam and Greg breached a charitable trust. That they were unjustly enriched. Unjustly enriched is a lawyer phrase for you got rich in a wrong way. Trial talk floated giant clawback numbers. One report said about 134 billion dollars of ill-gotten gains. Another headline said a 150 billion dollar fight. Those balloons were never the ending. The ending was a clock.

May 18, 2026. Nine jurors in Oakland. They talked for less than two hours. They said Elon waited too long. Statute of limitations. That means the law has a clock. If you start the fight after the clock dings, the court will not even hear the rest. Three years for the charity-trust claim. Two years for the enrichment claim. The jury found the clock had already dinged.

Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers took their finding and dismissed the case. She was not required to listen to an advisory jury. She did. She said there was a lot of evidence to support them. So the chair fight, in court, ended without a winner of the chair. It ended with a late stamp.

Elon posted that the judge and jury never ruled on the real story, only on a clock issue. He said there was no question Altman and Brockman enriched themselves by stealing a charity. He said the only question was when. He said he would appeal to the Ninth Circuit. That post is his thought, typed in public. It is not a secret. It is also not a court win.

OpenAI's side said the seeds of the for-profit were visible way back, even in 2017, so of course the clock dinged.

Here is the kid version of the ending. Elon wanted the chair. Sam kept it. Elon built a chair next door. Elon tried to buy the first chair. Sam said no thank you. Elon sued. The jury said you waited too long. The wooden seat is still in Sam's loft.

We cannot know every private feeling. We can know the pattern. Reach. Refusal. Exit. Copy. Insult. Lawsuit. Clock. That pattern is what Elon really thinks, shown with his hands. He thinks Sam took something that was supposed to be shared. Sam's papers say Elon wanted to own it. Both stories are about the same seat.

He wanted the chair. Sam kept it.

If you remember one joke, remember two famous men and one piece of wood. If you remember one date, remember September 2017, when Honest Thoughts met final straw. If you remember one later date, remember May 2026, when the clock beat the story. The chair did not move. The clock did.

A last honest limit. This cut cannot tell you what Elon whispers in a car. It can tell you he reached for control, got told no, left, cloned the toy, insulted the CEO, sued, and lost on time. That chain is the thought. Not a mind-reader. A pattern. Sam's chain would start in a different seat and use different mail. Leave that for a video that faces the other way. For this title, the wooden seat is enough. Empty at the start. Fought in 2017. Vacated in 2018. Filled by Sam. Wobbled for five days. Copied next door. Dragged into court. Still Sam's when the clock dinged.
Sam has his own mouth, and his own papers, and his own version of Elon. That is a different table, facing the other way. This cut stays on Elon's side of the wood.
